root_cause.text: The `__xfrm_state_delete` function in the xfrm subsystem uses mutable scalar value predicates (`x->km.seq` and `x->id.spi`) instead of list-state checks (`hlist_unhashed`) to guard list unhashing, and deletes list nodes using `hlist_del_rcu` instead of `hlist_del_init_rcu`, allowing inconsistent unhashing and double-deletion of `xfrm_state` list nodes via poisoned pointers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces `hlist_del_rcu` with `hlist_del_init_rcu` for the `bydst`, `bysrc`, `byseq`, and `byspi` lists, and replaces the value-based checks `if (x->km.seq)` and `if (x->id.spi)` with `if (!hlist_unhashed(&x->byseq))` and `if (!hlist_unhashed(&x->byspi))`. Additionally, the description notes that "a second __xfrm_state_delete() on the same object writes through LIST_POISON pprev" because the unhashes previously had no list-state predicates and did not re-initialize the list nodes.
